thread:
maya: CI is red for the docs linkcheck again, failing on some deep fragment links. anyone seen this pattern before?

alex: saw a few of these — looks like a heading normalization step in the MDX pipeline changed some hashes. quick snip from the CI log: 

ci-bot: linkcheck: ERROR http://docs.redwood.com/reference/runtime#memory-management -> 404 (fragment not found)

juniper: ah yep. there was a recent converter that squashes repeating punctuation in headings, e.g. \"Model: behavior!\" -> \"model-behavior\" instead of \"model-behavior-\" so anchors drift.

maya: ugh. that explains the mismatch with generated anchors. the PR that changed that was #1467 but it was meant to normalize emoji/soft-hyphen noise.

sam: could we add a quick redirect mapping or fallback resolver in the linkcheck step while we patch the headings? short-term fix > unblock release.

alex: agreed. propose we do two things: 1) backfill old-fragment -> new-fragment mapping in docs static config, 2) run a grep across code examples and SDK snippets for old anchors to update them.

juniper: I can add a small transform in the link-checker that tries a relaxed slug match if exact fragment fails — check for trailing punctuation or de-duped suffixes. but it's a bit hacky.

maya: hacky but ok as a stopgap. We should also assemble a list of top-visited pages to prioritize.

sam: here's a one-liner to find old fragment references in the repo: 

```
rg "#([a-z0-9\-]+)" docs/ --glob '!node_modules' -o | sed -E 's/^.*#/#/' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 40
```

alex: nice. I ran that and spotted ~12 instances in the SDK snippets where the anchor remained the old slug. I'll open a tiny follow-up PR to patch the snippets.

juniper: FYI the MkDocs build behaves slightly differently from Docusaurus — MkDocs slugify keeps underscores in some cases. we should normalize our slug algorithm across toolchains before rolling the converter changes.

maya: filed a short meta-issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1824 to track cross-tool slug spec and a migration plan.

sam: PRs: 1) docs: add linkcheck fallback (juniper) — WIP, 2) docs: snippet anchor cleanup (alex) — opened as #1489, 3) docs: redirect map for old anchors — i'll add as data file in static.

ci-bot: build: linkcheck job retriggered by @juniper — currently running.

maya: once linkcheck passes we should run the example apps smoke tests just to be safe (some examples embed full fragment URLs).

alex: quick note for reviewers — when updating snippets, keep inline code blocks identical except for the URL; don't change surrounding formatting or that will bloat the PR.

juniper: added the fallback logic as a toggle under docs-config, default off. I put a short comment: 

```
// Relaxed fragment resolution: attempts canonical slug variants (strip trailing punctuation, de-dupe numeric suffixes)
```

maya: lovely. can someone run the grep from sam and paste the top offenders in this thread so we can triage?

alex: pasted top offenders in the PR description of #1489. summary: runtime reference, quickstart anchors, and one tutorial page. I'll fix the snippet anchors this afternoon.

sam: after alex's PR lands, i'll add the redirect map file and then we can flip the fallback off and remove it in a week.

maya: plan sounds good. thanks all. small follow-ups: add a line to the docs contribution guide about not changing heading punctuation without coordinating with the slug spec, and ping the migration issue when you open PRs.

juniper: noted. leaving the WIP tag on my branch, ping me if you want the toggle on earlier.

ci-bot: linkcheck: SUCCESS for commit 7f3a2c9 (job #452)

maya: thanks — closing the loop. i'll update the release notes with a short blurb about heading normalization and the docs cleanup. :white_check_mark:
